static.note: A painted village with a HUD and a score line the game does not have. The drift is known, recorded in qa/thumbnails.mjs, and accepted — this baseline exists so the NEXT drift is not.

windup.note: Looked at beside the game at #167, level 1 and the levels with spikes, lava, belts, springs, a moving plate and an arc, in both palettes. Same place: mossy stone blocks with a grass cap, a green factory behind of big gears, pipes with flanges, lattice towers, a hanging lamp and a WINDUP banner, steel spikes, a glowing lava pool, electricity between two emitters, and belts with bright arrows. Accepted drift: the game's backdrop is darker and less saturated than the card's, so it stays behind the stone; its spikes, pool and arc are separate hazards in separate levels rather than one pit; and the robot, pickups, station, goal and HUD are still the old art, which #168 to #170 redraw.

lantern-keeper.note: Looked at beside the finished game at #175: every stage, the title and the forest path. Same place and the same figure: a layered forest with vines and leaves, mossy stone with a grass cap, a hooded keeper with a pack and a lantern held out, iron-and-glass lanterns glowing warm, a wooden DANGER sign, amber text on solid bars top and bottom. Accepted drift: the game is darker and its keeper smaller; its lanterns float rather than hang on chains; it has no rope ladder and no ruined stone pillars; and its bars show lanterns lit, the stage and the oil, where the card shows score, lives and health, which the game does not count.

pocket-dungeon.note: Baseline only: recorded as the game stood at #132, not compared against the card by eye. Its DMG art was unreachable when this was recorded; #134 wired the palette toggle, so the hashed art is now art a player can actually see.

cart-crate.note: Looked at beside the finished game at #165: all five worlds in both palettes, the title and the level select. The warehouse is the card's: grey-blue checkered floor, dark red-brown walls with a brick face, wooden crates, bright crosses in lit squares, the courier fox, and shelves and boxes round the room. Accepted drift: the card's room is larger than any one level's and fills its frame, where a level sits in a band of dark warehouse; the other four worlds are their own places in their own colours; and the game has a HUD bar top and bottom that the card does not.
